title: Hot dog sandwich, meat and poultry, on wheat bread

content.title: About
content.content: A hot dog sandwich consists of a meat‑and‑poultry sausage placed inside a split wheat bun. It is a popular fast‑food item often served with mustard, ketchup, mayonnaise and various vegetable toppings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first hot dog appeared in the United States in the late 19th century and quickly became street food.
Traditional American hot dogs are served in a wheat‑flour bun, but many countries use different types of bread.
There are more than 50 varieties of sausages used in hot dogs, including beef, pork, chicken and turkey.
In 1945 the first "National Hot Dog Day" was celebrated in the US, now observed annually.
Hot dogs are closely associated with baseball games and festivals.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Meat and poultry sausage provides complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat products are rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The sausage supplies B12, B6 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the bun and fats from the sausage delivers quick energy.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: Protein, fat and carbs together help maintain a feeling of fullness for longer.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed sausages often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: A high amount of saturated fat may contribute to cardiovascular disease when consumed frequently.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some sausages contain nitrites and other preservatives that are undesirable in large amounts.

items.title: Allergy to meat or gluten
items.content: People with allergies to certain meats or gluten may experience reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Hot dogs are calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hot dogs are usually eaten warm, topped with mustard, ketchup, mayonnaise, pickles, onions, cheese or salad. They can be heated on a grill, in an oven or in a microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared hot dog in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for no more than 2 days. Keep the sausage in its original packaging or an airtight container, and the bun in a dry place to prevent it from drying out.
